tool_input.command:
git add -A && git commit -m "Fix floating-point precision error in price-to-cents conversion

Use Math.round() when multiplying prices by 100 to convert to cents,
avoiding floating-point errors like 39.95 * 100 = 3995.0000000000005.

Fixes adding subscriptions with prices like 39.95 that previously failed
with 'price must be whole cents' validation error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"

git add src/locale.js src/money.js && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix floating-point precision error in price-to-cents conversion

Use Math.round() when multiplying prices by 100 to convert to cents,
avoiding floating-point errors like 39.95 * 100 = 3995.0000000000005.

Fixes adding subscriptions with prices like 39.95 that previously failed
with 'price must be whole cents' validation error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

claude.result:
Done! The bug is fixed. The issue was a floating-point precision error: when converting prices like `39.95` to cents by multiplying by 100, JavaScript produced `3995.0000000000005` instead of exactly `3995`, which failed the integer validation.

The fix wraps all three price-to-cents conversions with `Math.round()` to ensure proper integer results. Now all prices—including `39.95`—work correctly. ✓
